1	---
2	name: horizon
3	description: How to work inside an Archon Horizon workspace — orient from on-disk state, pick the highest-value formalization work, record progress as commits, and coordinate. Load this first; it points to the specialized skills for detail. Editable per workspace.
4	---
5	
6	You are working inside an **Archon Horizon** workspace: a place where AI agents
7	formalize mathematics in Lean 4 across one or more projects. This skill is the
8	map. It is deliberately short and **you can edit it** (it lives at
9	`.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md` in this workspace) — tune it to how you want to
10	work. It points to focused skills; load those on demand rather than up front.
11	
12	## You are a team; the workspace is where teams collaborate
13	
14	Think of your session as **one team**: you (the lead) plus the subagents you
15	spawn as your **workers**, with the tools and skills available to you. A
16	`horizon run` is your team working through its task. Other runs are **other
17	teams** working in parallel on the *same shared workspace* — one Lean project set,
18	one roadmap/board, one ledger, one inbox.
19	
20	You do not manage other teams and they do not manage you. You coordinate through
21	**shared state**, not meetings:
22	
23	- **The board (roadmap)** is the shared plan. Keep your items' status/owner/
24	  milestone current so other teams see what you hold and where it's going.
25	- **The inbox** is asynchronous messaging + memory across teams (skill:
26	  `horizon-inbox`): shared notes, per-task private items, and direct messages to
27	  another team.
28	- **Commits** are the durable record; reading recent ledger history tells you what
29	  other teams just produced (skill: `project-git`).
30	
31	Before you start, be aware of who else is live (see "Is another run live" below).
32	A short **synchronizer** digest is printed to stderr at the start of your CLI
33	commands. Its attention order is deliberate: `REQUIRED` active protections,
34	`ACTION` unread conversations, advisory unread inbox, then session/runtime and
35	other live runs. Read it; it is how you stay aware without asking anyone. A new
36	conversation or reply invalidates the digest cache immediately. If stderr is
37	redirected, the same protection/conversation lanes are the first `attention`
38	object in `horizon inbox list --json`.
39	
40	## Orient (pull state, don't assume it)
41	
42	**Start here:** your prompt says nothing about who ran before you. Usually
43	somebody did — often minutes ago, often on this same task, and their report was
44	written for you. Skill: `horizon-start` — one cheap pass that works out which
45	situation you were launched into (fresh run, hand-off from the session that just
46	finished, resume after a crash, or outside a run) and what to read for each.
47	
48	The workspace root is `$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT`; your shell may start in a member
49	project rather than at that root. The absolute path to this skill is
50	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL`. Live state is under
51	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/.archon-horizon/` and the manifest is
52	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/config.yaml`. Read what you need, when you need it — via the
53	`horizon` CLI (invoke it as `"$HORIZON_BIN" …`):
54	
55	- **Roadmap** — YOUR strategy sketch across *all* projects, kept as a nested
56	  outline. `"$HORIZON_BIN" roadmap list` renders the indented tree with per-parent
57	  progress (`active · 3/7 done`); `--focus <id>` shows one subtree, `--max-depth 0`
58	  the top level only. Structure it: nest sub-goals with `--parent`, keep your
59	  item's status current with `--status` and its strategy prose current with
60	  `--summary` / `--summary-file` (there is no `--strategy` flag). It doubles as
61	  the **project board**:
62	  set `--owner <team>` (who holds it), `--milestone <label>` (a free grouping tag,
63	  filter with `roadmap list --milestone <label>`), and pin concrete deliverables
64	  with `--pin-commit <sha>`. Roadmap commands print a **warning**
65	  when parent/child statuses disagree (all sub-items done but parent open, or a
66	  done parent with open children) — nothing is auto-corrected; you decide whether
67	  to fix it or leave it (it may be intentional). They also warn when too many
68	  milestones claim simultaneous `active` focus.
69	- **Tasks** — a specific piece of work, usually the one a human launched and is
70	  watching. `"$HORIZON_BIN" task …`. Task commands warn when the open queue grows
71	  beyond the advisory limit or a `running` status looks orphaned.
72	- **Inbox** — how teams talk across sessions and projects. Leave a note for the
73	  next session; read what past ones left. `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox …` (skill:
74	  `horizon-inbox`). Items can be **owned by your task** (private, e.g. your team's
75	  memory) or **shared with everyone** (the default); read-state is per-team, so
76	  `inbox list --mine --unread` is your team's fresh queue, and you can
77	  direct-message another team with `--to task:<id>`. Inbox commands warn when the
78	  open working set—especially `memory` and `info`—needs review.
79	- **Inbox attention order** — before edits, inspect all open `protection` items
80	  (standing constraints, whether read or unread), then open unread
81	  `conversation` items and reply or mark them read. Other kinds are advisory
82	  context. In an agent session an unqualified `inbox list` defaults to open items
83	  and sorts in this order; use an explicit status to audit history.
84	- **Conversation discipline** — use a conversation only when a reply/decision is
85	  expected. Search and reuse an open thread before starting one. Its initiator is
86	  a participant and owns closure: after consuming the answer, add a concise
87	  conclusion if needed and archive the thread. Reply to human-started threads but
88	  leave their closure to the human unless asked otherwise (skill: `horizon-inbox`).
89	- **Blueprint graph** — declaration dependencies and what's proved. `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> …` (skill: `hgraph`).
90	  Each node is also an **hgraph** file with attached comments/reviews —
91	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` ranks what to prove next, and node-scoped failure memory
92	  goes on the node itself (skill: `hgraph`).
93	- **Memory** — durable facts/dead-ends live in the inbox: read with
94	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --kind memory --json`, write with
95	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox add --kind memory --to horizon --body …`.
96	- **Usage** — your token/cost consumption this session and run, budget headroom,
97	  and recent rate-limit signals: `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json`. See
98	  "Pace yourself" below for how to act on it.
99	
100	## Your session's identity (environment variables)
101	
102	The harness exports these to every session — read them instead of guessing:
103	
104	| Variable | Meaning |
105	|---|---|
106	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT` | workspace root (use for `--root`-free CLI calls) |
107	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL` | absolute path to this `SKILL.md` (never resolve it relative to the shell cwd) |
108	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_RUN` | run id (e.g. `0163`) |
109	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION` | this session's name (e.g. `0002-horizon-T-1`) |
110	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION_DIR` | this session's directory (transcript, usage.json, report) |
111	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS` | which round this is (0-based) / the run's planned total |
112	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK_TITLE` | the task id / title (full body: `"$HORIZON_BIN" task show "$ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK" --json`) |
113	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_PROJECTS` | comma-separated projects this task spans |
114	| `HORIZON_BIN`, `HORIZON_GIT` | absolute paths to the CLI and the ledger-git wrapper |
115	| `HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR`, `HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE` | the workspace ledger repo + its work tree — `"$HORIZON_GIT" …` is shorthand for `git --git-dir "$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree "$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" …` |
116	
117	## Pace yourself (usage & interruption risk)
118	
119	Sessions end for reasons you don't control: rate limits, usage caps, budgets.
120	The defense is NOT to avoid work — it is to make interruption cheap:
121	
122	- **Commit at every coherent point** (plain git into the ledger, below). If
123	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` shows low budget headroom or recent
124	  `rate_limit`/`usage_limit` signals, commit what you have NOW and prefer
125	  finishing the piece in flight over opening a new front.
126	- If this is the run's **last round** (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` + 1 ==
127	  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS`), leave the workspace hand-off-clean: commit, update
128	  the roadmap/task status, and write the report as if nobody continues today.
129	- Interrupted anyway? Nothing is lost that was committed — the next session
130	  resumes from the ledger (see "Resuming" below).
131	
132	## One-shot discipline (important)
133	
134	This session runs to completion and is **not resumed** — you will not be re-invoked
135	when a background job finishes. So **run work in the foreground and block on it**
136	(builds, checks, subagents). Anything you leave running in the background, or leave
137	uncommitted, may be lost when the session ends. Commit early and often (below).
138	
139	## Pick the highest-value work
140	
141	Read the roadmap and the live Lean state, then commit to the most valuable next
142	piece. A node being large, multi-session, or blocked on missing mathlib
143	infrastructure is **not** a reason to skip it — start it, build the missing
144	lemma/definition yourself as project-local infrastructure, and push it as far as
145	you genuinely can. Prefer ambitious progress over defensive avoidance.
146	
147	If this session was launched on a specific task, make concrete progress on that
148	task's REAL objective — don't preemptively pivot to easy unrelated wins because
149	the objective is large. Leave a `"$HORIZON_BIN" task comment <task_id> --body …`
150	at each significant step. You own the task's terminal status (skill:
151	`task-status`): set `--status done` only when the objective is FULLY complete;
152	`blocked`/`failed` if genuinely stuck; set nothing if it's only partly advanced
153	(it returns to the queue).
154	
155	## Fresh-context checkpoints
156	
157	The old Ground pass is no longer a second orchestrator role, but independent
158	review is still part of convergence. Spawn the **`ground`** subagent at these
159	checkpoints:
160	
161	- before marking a multi-step task `done`;
162	- after every two substantive Horizon sessions on a long-running task;
163	- immediately after a strategy pivot, a broad workspace edit, or a surprising
164	  clean/build result.
165	
166	Give it the task/project scope and ask it to inspect the actual ledger diff,
167	blueprint graph, Lean state, roadmap, inbox, and reports with fresh context. It
168	is read-only on source and reports issues/memory; reconcile its findings before
169	continuing. Use **`work-reviewer`** for a narrow diff/proof audit and **`janitor`**
170	when the main concern is workspace hygiene. A one-session task may skip the
171	periodic checkpoint, but must still obtain a fresh-context review before a
172	terminal `done` claim.
173	
174	Schedule upkeep even when the last command did not print a warning. On a
175	multi-session run, dispatch **`janitor` at the start of every second Horizon
176	session** and before the final report; on a one-session task, dispatch it once
177	before claiming completion if the run touched roadmap, task, or inbox state.
178	Record the checkpoint in the report and wait for the helper before continuing.
179	If `janitor` is unavailable, ask **`ground`** for the same hygiene inspection;
180	Ground is read-only, so apply or explicitly record its findings yourself.
181	
182	## Warnings are work
183	
184	Commands report problems for a reason — never scroll past them. `lake build`
185	warnings, `horizon graph sync` warnings, roadmap consistency warnings, deprecation
186	notices from any tool: if your change caused it, **fix it now** (it is part of
187	the task); if it's pre-existing or caused by the tool/command itself, don't
188	silently ignore it — record it as a memory item, file an inbox `issue`, or
189	address it `--to human` when a human decision is needed. A warning that
190	survives your session should be one you *chose* to leave, with a trace saying
191	why.
192	
193	Collection-health warnings are a dispatch trigger, not background noise. When
194	`inbox`, `roadmap`, or `task` reports an overloaded queue, stale running item,
195	or status mismatch, pause the proof loop and spawn **`janitor`** with the
196	workspace scope. Wait for it, reconcile its report, rerun the command, and
197	record any warning that remains intentionally. Do this at most once for the
198	same warning in a session; a persistent warning still needs a report or inbox
199	issue rather than repeated no-op calls.
200	
201	## Do the work (Lean)
202	
203	For any Lean edit, load `lean-check` before touching the file and follow its
204	required LSP loop: query the target with `lean_diagnostic_messages` or
205	`lean_goal` before the first edit and after each subsequent edit. Keep `lake
206	build` for the final session boundary or a specifically required kernel check;
207	LSP is enough between edits and proof obligations. Use the narrowest `lake env
208	lean` fallback when LSP is unavailable, and do not duplicate that check when the
209	configured final build covers the same files.
210	
211	**Do not `grep` for a lemma.** Grep matches names you already guessed; it cannot
212	find the lemma whose name you don't know, and that is the one that costs you an
213	afternoon. This workspace indexes every declaration in every project *and* in
214	mathlib — query it:
215	
216	| You want | Use | Not |
217	|---|---|---|
218	| "does this lemma exist, anywhere?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" search "<words or name>" --json` | `grep -r` |
219	| "what's the lemma for this *statement*?" | LSP `lean_leansearch` (natural language) | guessing names |
220	| "what matches this *type*?" | LSP `lean_loogle` (`Nat → ?a → ?a`) | `grep` |
221	| "does something in scope close this goal?" | LSP `lean_local_search` / `lean_hover_info` | reading files |
222	| "what should I prove next?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` (ranked) | scanning the blueprint |
223	| "what does this node depend on / block?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> get label:<id>` | reading imports |
224	| "is the proof right?" | `lake env lean <file>` (narrowest faithful check) | `lean_diagnostic_messages` alone |
225	
226	`"$HORIZON_BIN" search` covers **your projects and mathlib together**, which is
227	its whole point: the premise you need is usually already in mathlib under a name
228	you would never have grepped for. One query costs a second; re-proving an
229	existing lemma costs a session. If it reports a library as unindexed, fix that
230	first (`lake build`, then `"$HORIZON_BIN" search --reindex`) rather than falling
231	back to grep.
232	
233	Grep is still the right tool for what it *is* good at: finding a known string, a
234	specific file, or every call site of a name you already have.
235	
236	- Search before proving — the lemma may already exist. Skill: `leansearch`.
237	- Use the **Lean LSP MCP** for tight proof feedback, then verify with the narrowest
238	  faithful `lake` / `lake env lean` check. Skill: `lean-check`.
239	- Use the DAG to choose and scope work, not just to report it. Skill: `hgraph`.
240	- When editing blueprint material, follow the house format. Skill: `blueprint-conventions`.
241	  The blueprint is timeless mathematics, never a formalization journal. Put Lean
242	  implementation notes, failed tactics, and declaration-specific progress on the
243	  corresponding hgraph node with `graph add comment`; do not insert
244	  "Formalization note" paragraphs into blueprint `.tex` files.
245	
246	## Read the other projects
247	
248	They are in this workspace for a reason: the same lemma, pattern, or dead end has
249	often already been worked out next door. `"$HORIZON_BIN" search` spans **all**
250	projects — an existing construction in another project is a lead, whether you
251	import it, copy the approach, or read its blueprint. `references/` holds the
252	original sources (skill: `references`). Staying inside your own project because
253	the task named it is how the workspace re-derives the same thing three times.
254	
255	## Delegating beyond your team (ask permission first)
256	
257	Your normal way to parallelize is **within** your team: spawn subagents/workers
258	(skill: `subagents`) and dispatch scoped work to them in the foreground. That
259	needs no permission.
260	
261	Launching work **outside** your team — creating new tasks for other teams, or
262	spawning a whole new `horizon run` — is different: it spends the user's compute
263	and accounts, so it is **off by default**. Before you even consider it, read the
264	standing consent: `"$HORIZON_BIN" permissions --json`. It reports
265	`allow_launch_tasks`, `allow_launch_runs`, `max_parallel_sessions`, any declared
266	`accounts`, and free-form notes the user left (e.g. which account to prefer, when
267	limits reset). If both `allow_*` are false (the default), **do not** create tasks
268	or launch runs on the user's behalf — instead leave an inbox item `--to human`
269	proposing the delegation and why. Only when a flag is enabled may you act within
270	its stated caps, and follow the account/usage notes the user recorded.
271	
272	## Record progress = commit (this is how progress is read)
273	
274	Your commits — message + diff — are the durable record of what you did; the
275	dashboard reads progress from them. Commit coherent progress yourself with plain
276	`git` into the workspace ledger. Skill: `project-git` (use `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m …`
277	or the explicit `--git-dir/--work-tree` form; provenance trailers are auto-stamped).
278	
279	Write **semantic, math-first** messages that say what you proved/built. Prefer
280	staging explicit files over `add -A`. Beyond commits:
281	
282	- Update the **roadmap** with coarse status (`--status`) and strategy prose
283	  (`--summary`), not a re-narration of the diff.
284	- Use the **inbox** to hand off to the next/other sessions; record durable dead-ends
285	  as **memory**.
286	
287	Before your final report, do one boundary-maintenance pass. Re-read the task's
288	`roadmap_refs` and `inbox_refs`; update each roadmap milestone whose status or
289	strategy changed, add a concise mathematical comment for a key advance, and
290	archive or complete open inbox items your work actually resolved. Also scan the
291	remaining open inbox for consumed temporary/info/memory items and archive those
292	that are now stale. Never archive a standing protection merely to make the list
293	shorter. In particular, review every open conversation your task started: archive
294	answered threads and leave a concrete blocker on any that must stay open. This
295	pass is part of completing the work, not optional janitor follow-up.
296	
297	## Resuming after an interruption
298	
299	State lives on disk, so a fresh session (even on another account) continues
300	cheaply. Working out *whether* you're resuming, and what to read if you are, is
301	the `horizon-start` skill — load it at the start of the session. The essentials:
302	
303	- **Why did the last run stop?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` includes a
304	  `paused` field (from `runs/<id>/paused.json`) with the reason (usage limit,
305	  budget, …) and the exact resume command; `recent_failure_reasons` shows
306	  rate-limit signals. A paused/killed run resumes with
307	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" run --resume <id>`.
308	- **What was in flight?** Read recent ledger history (`project-git` skill:
309	  `git log` + `git show` by `Archon-Session` trailer) and the previous
310	  session's transcript/report under `.archon-horizon/runs/`. A horizon session
311	  directory with **no `report.md`** is one that was killed mid-flight.
312	- **Is another run live on this workspace?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" ps` lists runs
313	  holding a process (the ledger is one shared branch — be aware of parallel
314	  writers); it also flags zombie markers and stalled runs. A run registers a
315	  `runs/<id>/process.json` marker (pid/host) at start and removes it on clean
316	  exit; `ps` decides liveness by probing the pid on the local host (a marker whose
317	  pid is dead is a reap-able zombie, a live pid idle for a long time is "stalled").
318	  The synchronizer surfaces the same "other runs live" signal at command start, so
319	  you usually don't need to call `ps` explicitly.
320	
321	## Final report (your last message)
322	
323	Your final message is saved as the session's report — a human or the next
324	session should understand the session from it without opening raw logs.
325	Recommended sections: `## Summary`, `## Progress`, `## Issues`,
326	`## Why I stopped`, `## Next` (keep at least `## Progress` and
327	`## Why I stopped`). In `## Progress`, one inline `-` bullet per file/target,
328	e.g. `- FileA.lean: 4 sorries -> 3; closed the base case.` In `## Why I
329	stopped`, say plainly whether the objective is fully complete, partly advanced,
330	or blocked — and why. Always mention build failures, broken proofs, blocked
331	dependencies, and checks that failed or were not run. If a plausible next
332	action fits in the session's scope, take it before stopping — a clean commit is
333	not by itself a reason to stop.
334	
335	## Cleaning up the work (you decide, via subagents)
336

338	and the **`ground`** subagent is the scheduled fresh-context checkpoint when the

3	description: Work out which situation you were launched into — first round of a fresh run, a hand-off from the horizon session that just finished, a resume after a crash or pause, or a session outside any run — and pull exactly the context that situation calls for. 5	
6	Your prompt carries the task and nothing else: no history, no word about who ran
7	before you or how they ended. That is deliberate — state is pulled, not pushed
8	(the `horizon` skill's stance). But it means a session that starts working
9	immediately is guessing. Usually somebody *was* here before you, often minutes
10	ago, and their report was written for you.
11	
12	This skill is the first pass: four cheap reads, a guess at the situation, then
13	the context that situation actually calls for. Budget a couple of minutes, not a
14	tenth of the session.

18	```bash
19	ls "$ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION_DIR/.."     # sibling sessions in THIS run
20	"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json             # `paused` (why the last run stopped) + `recent_failure_reasons`
21	"$HORIZON_BIN" ps                       # is another run live on this workspace RIGHT NOW?
22	"$HORIZON_GIT" log --oneline -15        # what actually landed recently

26	like:

28	```
29	0001-system            ← orchestrator bookkeeping (commits, integration), not an agent
30	0002-horizon-PET.5     ← a horizon session; meta.json + transcript.jsonl + usage.json
31	0003-system
32	0004-horizon-PET.5     ← ...you, probably

36	
37	- **`report.md` present** → that session finished on its own terms and wrote you
38	  a hand-off. **`report.md` absent** → it was killed mid-flight. This is the
39	  single most informative bit on disk.

41	  `model`. `ended_at` against the current time tells you whether "recent" means
42	  four minutes ago or last week.

44	## Which situation am I in?
45	
46	Work down the list; the first match is your best guess.
47	
48	**An earlier horizon sibling has no `report.md`** → *resume after a crash or
49	kill.* Its work is half-done and possibly half-committed. Read its commits in
50	the ledger first (they are the part that survived), then the tail of its
51	transcript to see what it was in the middle of — `usage --json` `paused` gives
52	the reason it died (usage limit, budget, auth), and `recent_failure_reasons`
53	shows rate-limit pressure that may still be there. Trust the ledger over the
54	transcript: anything it did not commit is gone, no matter what it said it was
55	doing. If the dead session shares your `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK`, you are continuing
56	its exact work — pick up its front rather than opening a new one.
57	
58	**An earlier horizon sibling has a `report.md`** → *hand-off from the session
59	that just finished.* The common case. Read that report first — its `## Next` and
60	`## Why I stopped` were written for exactly this moment — then its commits, then
61	any inbox items addressed to horizon since its `ended_at`. Do not re-derive what
62	it already established; do not redo a piece it says is done without checking the
63	ledger.
64	
65	**`ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` is `0` and no horizon sibling exists** → *first agent
66	of the run.* Nobody handed you anything **in this run** — but the workspace is
67	almost never greenfield. Earlier runs live under `.archon-horizon/runs/`; the
68	roadmap, the inbox and the ledger carry their conclusions. Skim the roadmap and
69	recent ledger history before deciding a strategy that a previous run already
70	tried and rejected.

93	  (`"$HORIZON_BIN" task show "$ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK" --json`). Skill:
94	  `horizon-inbox`.

8	/-!
9	# Section drop and the `H¹` peel, on the dévissage sequence
10	
11	Cluster P asks for the *section-drop* results and for `H¹` vanishing.  This file supplies the
12	drop layer and the exact statement of the peel, both **unconditionally** on the χ-ledger's own
13	carrier: the only hypotheses are the five curve binders `ChiLedger.lean` already runs on
14	(`Field K`, `SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1`, `IsIntegral`, `QuasiCompact`, and the two
15	`Module.Finite` cohomology instances, which `ChiCurve`/`Finiteness` discharge at a curve).
16	
17	Everything comes off the six-term slice of the dévissage sequence
18	`0 → 𝒪(D − x) → 𝒪(D) → sky_x J → 0` (`Ledger/ChiSlice.lean`), whose third term has
19	`H¹ = 0` because it is a skyscraper.  Two slots of that slice are the whole content:
20	
21	* `H⁰(𝒪(D − x)) ↪ H⁰(𝒪(D))` — `injective_map_f_zero`;
22	* `H¹(𝒪(D − x)) ↠ H¹(𝒪(D))` — `surjective_map_f _ 1`, available because `H¹(sky) = 0`.
23	
24	## What is proved
25	
26	* `h0_divisorSheaf_le_of_le`, `h1_divisorSheaf_le_of_le` — monotonicity of `h⁰` and
27	  antitonicity of `h¹` along a *single dévissage step*.
28	* `h0_sub_point_le`, `h0_le_h0_sub_point_add_residueDeg` — the **two-sided section drop**
29	  `h⁰(𝒪(D − x)) ≤ h⁰(𝒪(D)) ≤ h⁰(𝒪(D − x)) + [κ(x) : K]`.
30	* `h0_sub_h0_sub_point_add_h1_sub_h1_sub_point` — the drop **identity**: the `h⁰` gain and
31	  the `h¹` loss add up to the residue degree exactly.
32	* `subsingleton_hModule_one_of_subsingleton_sub_point` (★ the peel) — `H¹` vanishing
33	  **propagates upward** across a dévissage step: if `H¹(𝒪(D − x)) = 0` then `H¹(𝒪(D)) = 0`.
34	  AJC's *adelic* lane takes this as a hypothesis on its own carrier
35	  (`Adelic/BoundedVanishing.lean`'s peel datum, discharged only off the overlap); on the ledger
36	  carrier it is a theorem of the slice.  It is **not new to the workspace**: AJCR proves the
37	  same chain in `RiemannRoch/FLVClass.lean` (`peel_single`, `peel_nsmul_single`,
38	  `peel_effective`).  See the provenance note on `subsingleton_hModule_one_add_effective`.
39	* `subsingleton_hModule_one_of_le` (★) — the same statement along **any** divisor increase
40	  `D₀ ≤ D`, by dévissage induction: `H¹` vanishing is **upward closed on the effective cone
41	  above `D₀`**.  Together with `chi_divisorSheaf` this turns one vanishing into the exact
42	  Riemann–Roch equality `h⁰(𝒪(D)) = χ(𝒪_X) + deg D` at every `D ≥ D₀`
43	  (`h0_divisorSheaf_of_subsingleton_of_le`), and makes the section drop *exact*
44	  (`h0_eq_h0_sub_point_add_residueDeg_of_subsingleton`).
45	
46	**The peel chain uses no finiteness at all.**  Eleven of the nineteen declarations below `omit` both
47	`Module.Finite` cohomology instances: surjectivity of a map is not a dimension count.  That
48	is also why the peel is stated on `Subsingleton (H¹ …)` rather than on `h¹ … = 0` — the
49	latter is vacuously true for an infinite-dimensional `H¹`, since `Module.finrank` reads `0`
50	there, so the `Subsingleton` form is both the stronger statement and the honest one.  The
51	`h¹`-spellings (`h1_le_h1_sub_point`, `h1_eq_zero_of_h1_sub_point_eq_zero`) do need the
52	finiteness, and they carry it.
53	
54	## What this does NOT supply — the three cluster-P items, kept apart
55	
56	Read this before quoting anything above as "uniform vanishing":
57	
58	1. **Single-field bounded vanishing** — "there is `N` such that `deg D ≥ N` implies
59	   `h¹(𝒪(D)) = 0`".  NOT proved here and not implied by anything here.  The peel moves
60	   vanishing *up the divisor order* `D₀ ≤ D`, and a divisor of large *degree* need not
61	   dominate `D₀`; the two are different partial data.  (The adelic lane states exactly this
62	   gap as `Adelic.coneVanishing_iff_base_and_peel`; the present file discharges its *peel*
63	   half on this carrier, not its base half.)  A base vanishing `H¹(𝒪(D₀)) = 0` at even one
64	   `D₀` is an input nothing in this file produces.
65	
66	   **Where the base actually stands, and a correction.**  Inside *this project's* Ledger tree
67	   the base is unavailable: `H¹(𝒪) = 0` at `ℙ¹` would need `ledgerGenus (Adelic.p1Over k) = 0`,
68	   which `Ledger/NonVacuity.lean` explicitly does *not* prove (it proves the hypothesis bundle
69	   is inhabited — a different claim), and the tree's only `H¹`-vanishing producer,
70	   `AffineVanishing.Scheme.subsingleton_moduleKSheaf_hModule_one`, requires `[IsAffine X]` and
71	   so cannot reach a proper curve at all.
72	
73	   **But the base is NOT open in the workspace.**  The sibling project
74	   `Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild` proves a base vanishing on this very carrier:
75	   `RiemannRoch/FLVVanishing.subsingleton_hModule_divisorSheaf_one_of_isFinite_toP1` (:302)
76	   gives, for a finite dominant `π : Y ⟶ ℙ¹` compatible with the structure maps and any `D`,
77	   an `n₀` with `H¹(𝒪(D + n·F)) = 0` for all `n ≥ n₀`, where `F` is the fibre divisor.  An
78	   earlier version of this docstring said the base was open "at every curve"; that was measured
79	   only in AJC's own tree and is **false as a statement about the workspace** — the same
80	   cone-scoping error this lane has now made repeatedly.  What AJC lacks is the *import*: AJCR's
81	   fibre-divisor and finite-map-to-`ℙ¹` layer is not present here.  So the honest gap is a
82	   **port**, not an open problem, and `exists_bound_of_cofinal_vanishing` is the right shape to
83	   receive it — AJCR's conclusion is a tower `D + n·F`, which is exactly a cofinal family.
84	2. **Extension-uniformity** — a bound uniform over finite extensions `K'/K`.  Untouched:
85	   no statement here quantifies over a second field, and `CurveDivisor`/`residueDeg` are
86	   pinned to the single base field `K`.
87	3. **Global generation** — that `𝒪(D)` is generated by its global sections.  Untouched on
88	   *this* carrier: no evaluation map appears in this file.  Note that
89	   `h0_eq_h0_sub_point_add_residueDeg_of_subsingleton` below is a statement about
90	   **dimensions**, not about surjectivity of evaluation: it says the drop equals the residue
91	   degree, which is the numerical *shadow* of generation at `x`, not generation itself.  The
92	   adelic lane does prove the bridge between them (`Adelic/GlobalGeneration.lean`:
93	   `generatedAt_of_evalMap_surjective` and `evalMap_surjective`), but on its own `degK`
94	   carrier and gated on `hledger` plus two vanishings; nothing here transports it, because
95	   this file has no evaluation map to feed it.
96	
97	So the honest summary: on this carrier the **peel** is unconditional at every closed point,
98	the **base** is not supplied, and the **degree threshold** is reduced to one named cofinality
99	hypothesis (`exists_bound_of_cofinal_vanishing`) that remains open.
100	-/

171	/-! ## Monotonicity of `h⁰` and antitonicity of `h¹` across one step -/
172	
173	section Step
174	
175	variable {x : X} (hx : x ≠ genericPoint X) (D : X.CurveDivisor)
176	
177	/-- **`h⁰` grows along a dévissage step**: `h⁰(𝒪(D − x)) ≤ h⁰(𝒪(D))`, from injectivity at
178	the left end of the slice. -/
179	theorem h0_sub_point_le :
180	    Sheaf.h0 (X.divisorSheaf K (D - CurveDivisor.single hx 1)) ≤
181	      Sheaf.h0 (X.divisorSheaf K D) := by
182	  have hinj := injective_hModule_zero_divisorSheafLE K hx D
183	  haveI : Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (devissageSES K hx D).X₂ 0) :=
184	    inferInstanceAs (Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (X.divisorSheaf K D) 0))
185	  exact LinearMap.finrank_le_finrank_of_injective (f := Sheaf.HModule.map
186	    (devissageSES K hx D).f 0) hinj
187	
188	/-- **`h¹` drops along a dévissage step**: `h¹(𝒪(D)) ≤ h¹(𝒪(D − x))`, from surjectivity of
189	the peel map. -/
190	theorem h1_le_h1_sub_point :
191	    Sheaf.h1 (X.divisorSheaf K D) ≤
192	      Sheaf.h1 (X.divisorSheaf K (D - CurveDivisor.single hx 1)) := by
193	  have hsurj := surjective_hModule_one_divisorSheafLE K hx D
194	  haveI : Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (devissageSES K hx D).X₁ 1) :=
195	    inferInstanceAs (Module.Finite K
196	      (Sheaf.HModule (X.divisorSheaf K (D - CurveDivisor.single hx 1)) 1))
197	  exact LinearMap.finrank_le_finrank_of_surjective (f := Sheaf.HModule.map
198	    (devissageSES K hx D).f 1) hsurj
199	
200	/-- **The section drop is at most the residue degree**:
201	`h⁰(𝒪(D)) ≤ h⁰(𝒪(D − x)) + [κ(x) : K]`.  Read off the χ-ledger step together with
202	`h¹(𝒪(D)) ≤ h¹(𝒪(D − x))`: the Euler characteristic gains exactly `[κ(x) : K]`, and the
203	`h¹` term can only help. -/
204	theorem h0_le_h0_sub_point_add_residueDeg :
205	    Sheaf.h0 (X.divisorSheaf K D) ≤
206	      Sheaf.h0 (X.divisorSheaf K (D - CurveDivisor.single hx 1)) + X.residueDeg K x := by
207	  have hstep := chi_step K hx D
208	  have hmono := h1_le_h1_sub_point K hx D
209	  rw [Sheaf.chi, Sheaf.chi] at hstep
210	  omega
211	
212	/-- **The drop identity**: the `h⁰` gain plus the `h¹` loss is exactly the residue degree,
213	`(h⁰(𝒪(D)) − h⁰(𝒪(D − x))) + (h¹(𝒪(D − x)) − h¹(𝒪(D))) = [κ(x) : K]`.  This is `chi_step`
214	rearranged, stated in ℤ so that both differences are honest. -/
215	theorem h0_sub_h0_sub_point_add_h1_sub_h1_sub_point :
216	    ((Sheaf.h0 (X.divisorSheaf K D) : ℤ) -
217	        Sheaf.h0 (X.divisorSheaf K (D - CurveDivisor.single hx 1))) +
218	      ((Sheaf.h1 (X.divisorSheaf K (D - CurveDivisor.single hx 1)) : ℤ) -
219	        Sheaf.h1 (X.divisorSheaf K D)) = X.residueDeg K x := by
220	  have hstep := chi_step K hx D
221	  rw [Sheaf.chi, Sheaf.chi] at hstep
222	  omega
223	
224	end Step

232	/-- **The peel** (★): `H¹` vanishing propagates *up* one dévissage step.  If
233	`H¹(𝒪(D − x)) = 0` then `H¹(𝒪(D)) = 0`, because `H¹(𝒪(D − x)) ↠ H¹(𝒪(D))`.

235	This is the exact statement the adelic lane carries as an unproved peel-surjectivity datum.

238	theorem subsingleton_hModule_one_of_subsingleton_sub_point {x : X}
239	    (hx : x ≠ genericPoint X) (D : X.CurveDivisor)
240	    (h : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (X.divisorSheaf K (D - CurveDivisor.single hx 1)) 1)) :

242	  have hsurj := surjective_hModule_one_divisorSheafLE K hx D
243	  haveI hsub : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (devissageSES K hx D).X₁ 1) := h
244	  exact ⟨fun a b => by
245	    obtain ⟨a', rfl⟩ := hsurj a
246	    obtain ⟨b', rfl⟩ := hsurj b
247	    rw [Subsingleton.elim a' b']⟩
248

252	    (h : Sheaf.h1 (X.divisorSheaf K (D - CurveDivisor.single hx 1)) = 0) :

259	/-! ## Upward closure of `H¹` vanishing on the cone above a divisor
260	
261	The single-step peel iterates.  The induction is `CurveDivisor.induction_devissage` applied
262	to the *difference* `D - D₀`, whose effectivity is what "above `D₀`" means; the predicate is

272	    (h : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (X.divisorSheaf K B) 1)) :
273	    Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (X.divisorSheaf K (B + CurveDivisor.single hx 1)) 1) := by
274	  refine subsingleton_hModule_one_of_subsingleton_sub_point K hx
275	    (B + CurveDivisor.single hx 1) ?_
276	  have heq : B + CurveDivisor.single hx 1 - CurveDivisor.single hx 1 = B := by abel
277	  rwa [heq]
278	
279	omit [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (X.moduleKSheaf K) 0)]
280	  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (X.moduleKSheaf K) 1)] in
281	/-- **Peeling a multiple of a point**: `H¹(𝒪(A)) = 0` forces `H¹(𝒪(A + n·x)) = 0`. -/
282	theorem subsingleton_hModule_one_add_nsmul_single {x : X} (hx : x ≠ genericPoint X)
283	    (A : X.CurveDivisor) (n : ℕ)
284	    (h : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (X.divisorSheaf K A) 1)) :
285	    Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (X.divisorSheaf K (A + n • CurveDivisor.single hx 1)) 1) := by
286	  induction n with
287	  | zero => rwa [zero_nsmul, add_zero]
288	  | succ n ih =>
289	    have hstep := subsingleton_hModule_one_add_single K hx
290	      (A + n • CurveDivisor.single hx 1) ih
291	    have heq : A + n • CurveDivisor.single hx 1 + CurveDivisor.single hx 1
292	        = A + (n + 1) • CurveDivisor.single hx 1 := by
293	      rw [succ_nsmul]; abel
294	    rwa [heq] at hstep
295	
296	omit [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (X.moduleKSheaf K) 0)]
297	  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (X.moduleKSheaf K) 1)] in
298	/-- **Effective peeling**: `H¹(𝒪(A)) = 0` forces `H¹(𝒪(A + E)) = 0` for every effective `E`.
299	Induction on the size of the support of `E`, one multiplicity block at a time.

302	new result.  `Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild`'s `RiemannRoch/FLVClass.lean` already has

312	(`subsingleton_hModule_one_of_le`), the two-sided section drop, the drop identity, exact
313	Riemann–Roch on the order-cone, and the cofinality reduction.  The peel chain itself is
314	duplicated mathematics, kept here only because AJC cannot import AJCR. -/
315	theorem subsingleton_hModule_one_add_effective (A E : X.CurveDivisor) (hE : 0 ≤ E)
316	    (h : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (X.divisorSheaf K A) 1)) :
317	    Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (X.divisorSheaf K (A + E)) 1) := by
318	  suffices H : ∀ (n : ℕ) (E : X.CurveDivisor), 0 ≤ E → (toFinsupp E).support.card = n →
319	      Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (X.divisorSheaf K (A + E)) 1) from H _ E hE rfl
320	  intro n
321	  induction n with
322	  | zero =>
323	    intro E hE hc
324	    have hE0 : E = 0 := Finsupp.support_eq_empty.mp (Finset.card_eq_zero.mp hc)
325	    rwa [hE0, add_zero]
326	  | succ n ih =>
327	    intro E hE hc
328	    classical
329	    have hne : (toFinsupp E).support.Nonempty := by
330	      rw [← Finset.card_pos, hc]; exact Nat.succ_pos n
331	    obtain ⟨p, hp⟩ := hne
332	    set b : ℤ := toFinsupp E p with hb
333	    have hb_nonneg : 0 ≤ b := Finsupp.le_def.mp hE p
334	    set E' : X.CurveDivisor := Finsupp.erase p (toFinsupp E) with hE'
335	    have hdecomp : CurveDivisor.single p.2 b + E' = E := by
336	      rw [hE', hb]; exact Finsupp.single_add_erase p (toFinsupp E)
337	    have hE'nonneg : 0 ≤ E' := by
338	      rw [hE']
339	      refine Finsupp.le_def.mpr (fun q => ?_)
340	      by_cases hq : q = p
341	      · subst hq; rw [Finsupp.erase_same]; rfl
342	      · rw [Finsupp.erase_ne hq]; exact Finsupp.le_def.mp hE q
343	    have hcard : (toFinsupp E').support.card = n := by
344	      have hEF : toFinsupp E' = Finsupp.erase p (toFinsupp E) := rfl
345	      rw [hEF, Finsupp.support_erase, Finset.card_erase_of_mem hp, hc, Nat.succ_sub_one]

# FLV-2(b) + FLV-3 — the H¹-quotient identification and the fibrewise large-twist vanishing

The heart of the Wave-4 fibrewise-large-twist-vanishing campaign
(`informal/w4-flv-worksheet.md` §§2.1, 2.3, bricks FLV-2(b) and FLV-3), for the curve
bundle `Y` (integral, smooth of relative dimension one and quasi-compact over a field `K`)
with a dominant affine morphism `π : Y ⟶ ℙ¹` and its fiber divisor
`F = fiberWeilDivisor π` (`AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.FLVFiberToolkit`).

## The identification (FLV-2(b))

On the affine two-cover `V₀ = π⁻¹ D₊(X₀)`, `V₁ = π⁻¹ D₊(X₁)`, the general-coefficients
two-cover carrier `Scheme.twoCoverH1LinearEquiv` — its two affine vanishing instances
discharged by the quasi-coherence packaging of `AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.FLVQcoh` —
computes `H¹` of the twisted sheaf `𝒪(D + n·F)` as a cokernel of section modules. This
file identifies that cokernel with a quotient of the **fixed** ambient overlap lattice
`N = 𝒪(D)(V₀ ⊓ V₁)` (constant in `n`, by the landed overlap-constancy
`divisorSections_add_nsmul_fiberWeilDivisor_overlap`) by the fiber lattice `Aₙ` of
`AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.FLVLattice`, comapped through `N.subtype` — the one
submodule-of-submodule bridge of the campaign, paid once behind the named submodule
`AlgebraicGeometry.fiberLatticeOverlap` (worksheet discipline (2)):

`AlgebraicGeometry.fiberLatticeH1Equiv :
  HModule (𝒪(D + n·F)) 1 ≃ₗ[K] N ⧸ fiberLatticeOverlap π D n`.

## The endgame (FLV-3)

`Submodule.eventually_eq_top_of_monotone_of_iSup_eq_top` is the pure linear-algebra
stabilization: an increasing `ℕ`-chain of submodules with join `⊤` whose base has
Noetherian quotient is eventually `⊤` (images in the quotient by the base stabilize by
`monotone_stabilizes_iff_noetherian`, and the stabilized value must be everything).
Instantiated with `Aₙ` inside `N`:

* the chain is increasing (`fiberLattice_mono`) and exhausts `N` (`iSup_fiberLattice`,
  THE EXHAUSTION of FLV-1 — pole clearing at the finite fiber over `[1 : 0]`);
* `N ⧸ A₀` is finite-dimensional: it is `H¹(𝒪(D + 0·F))` through the identification, and
  every divisor sheaf has finite `H¹` by the landed dévissage
  (`moduleFinite_hModule_divisorSheaf_one`, `AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.ChiFiniteness`)
  — the only place the base finiteness (properness) inputs enter;

so `Aₙ = ⊤` for all large `n`, and through the identification the twisted `H¹` is a
subsingleton — **the fibrewise large-twist vanishing**
(`AlgebraicGeometry.subsingleton_hModule_divisorSheaf_one_of_isDominant_toP1`): per-class
`n₀`, no duality, no `R¹f_*`. The worksheet-shaped form for a finite dominant `π`
compatible with the structure morphisms
(`subsingleton_hModule_divisorSheaf_one_of_isFinite_toP1`) discharges the base
`H¹(𝒪_Y)`-finiteness input from finiteness of `π`
(`moduleFinite_hModule_one_of_isFinite_toP1`).
-/

/-!
# The degree homomorphism on the Čech Picard group

For the curve bundle `X` (integral, smooth of relative dimension one and quasi-compact over
a field `K`, with finite `H⁰`/`H¹` of the structure sheaf — the two instance hypotheses
through which properness enters), this file builds the **degree homomorphism** on the Čech
Picard group and records the E-i..E-iii interface of the degree lane
(`informal/degree-pic0-recon.md` §3 G-D3, `informal/deg-d2-meromorphic-worksheet.md` W5).

The anchored class map `CurveDivisor.picClass K : X.CurveDivisor → X.CechPic` of the
meromorphic bridge (`Picard/DivisorClassMeromorphic.lean`) is surjective, with fibres the
principal divisors. The degree of a Weil divisor is class-invariant: two divisors of equal
class differ by a principal divisor (extraction `(X)`, `CurveDivisor.exists_divOf_of_picClass_eq`)
and principal divisors have degree zero (`deg_divOf`, the χ-ledger), so `deg` descends to a
homomorphism on classes.

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.classDeg` — the degree homomorphism `Additive X.CechPic →+ ℤ`:
  `classDeg 𝒪(D) = deg D` for any Weil divisor `D`. The carrier `Additive X.CechPic →+ ℤ`
  is chosen so that a *value* `classDeg L` is a genuine integer: `X.CechPic` is a `CommGroup`
  (line-bundle tensor) and the degrees form the additive group `ℤ`, so the idiomatic
  packaging of "a group homomorphism from the multiplicative Picard group to the additive
  group `ℤ`" is an `AddMonoidHom` out of `Additive X.CechPic`. Because `Additive X.CechPic`
  is definitionally `X.CechPic`, the interface statements below read literally, and
  `map_zero`/`map_add`/`map_neg`/`map_zsmul` come for free from the bundled hom.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.classDeg_picClass` (**E-i**, normalization): `classDeg 𝒪(D) = deg D`,
  the definitional anchor, for *every* Weil divisor `D`.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.classDeg_mul` (**E-ii**, homomorphism):
  `classDeg (L · L') = classDeg L + classDeg L'`.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.chi_divisorSheaf_classDeg` (**E-iii**, χ-connection):
  `χ(𝒪(D)) = χ(𝒪_X) + classDeg 𝒪(D)`.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.chi_divisorSheaf_eq_of_picClass_eq`: the Euler characteristic of a class
  is well-defined — `𝒪(D) = 𝒪(D') → χ(𝒪(D)) = χ(𝒪(D'))` — via the multiplication
  isomorphism `mulEquivDivisorSheaf` and `chi_congr` (no finiteness needed).
* `AlgebraicGeometry.classDeg_divisorClass`: the deg-D1 divisor class map has the same degree,
  `classDeg (divisorClass K D) = deg D`, through the collapse `divisorClass_eq_picClass`.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.chi_divisorSheaf_classDeg_curve`: the curve form
  `χ(𝒪(D)) = 1 − genus C + classDeg 𝒪(D)` on the challenge curve.

The recon's E-i pushforward-rank reading (`classDeg 𝒪(D) = dim_K Γ(𝒪_D)` for *effective*
`D`, the Dedekind colength of the structure sheaf of the subscheme `D`) is a separate
statement about global sections of `𝒪_D`; it is *not* this brick's definitional anchor
(`classDeg 𝒪(D) = deg D`) and is deferred to a later node.
-/

/-- **The fiber lattice inside the fixed ambient overlap module** (the FLV-2(b) bridge
submodule): the Čech `H¹` denominator `Aₙ = 𝒪(D + n·F)(V₀) ⊔ 𝒪(D + n·F)(V₁)` of
`AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.FLVLattice`, viewed as a submodule of the fixed ambient
`N = 𝒪(D)(V₀ ⊓ V₁)` through `N.subtype` (`fiberLattice_le_overlap` certifies the
containment). All submodule-of-submodule bookkeeping of the campaign is sealed behind
this definition. -/
noncomputable def fiberLatticeOverlap (D : Y.CurveDivisor) (n : ℕ) :
    Submodule K (divisorSections K D (fiberChart₀ π ⊓ fiberChart₁ π)) :=
  (fiberLattice π D n).comap
    (divisorSections K D (fiberChart₀ π ⊓ fiberChart₁ π)).subtype

lemma mem_fiberLatticeOverlap {D : Y.CurveDivisor} {n : ℕ}
    {s : divisorSections K D (fiberChart₀ π ⊓ fiberChart₁ π)} :
    s ∈ fiberLatticeOverlap π D n ↔ (s : Y.functionField) ∈ fiberLattice π D n :=
  Iff.rfl

/-- The fiber lattice inside the ambient overlap module is an increasing chain
(`fiberLattice_mono` comapped). -/
lemma fiberLatticeOverlap_mono (D : Y.CurveDivisor) :
    Monotone (fiberLatticeOverlap π D) := fun _ _ h =>
  Submodule.comap_mono ((monotone_nat_of_le_succ (fiberLattice_mono π D)) h)

/-- **Exhaustion inside the ambient** (`iSup_fiberLattice` comapped): the increasing chain
`Aₙ` fills the whole of `N = 𝒪(D)(V₀ ⊓ V₁)`. -/
theorem iSup_fiberLatticeOverlap (D : Y.CurveDivisor) :
    ⨆ n, fiberLatticeOverlap π D n = ⊤ := by
  rw [eq_top_iff]
  rintro s -
  have hs : (s : Y.functionField) ∈ ⨆ n, fiberLattice π D n := by
    rw [iSup_fiberLattice π D]
    exact s.2
  obtain ⟨m, hm⟩ := (Submodule.mem_iSup_of_directed _
    (monotone_nat_of_le_succ (fiberLattice_mono π D)).directed_le).mp hs
  exact Submodule.mem_iSup_of_mem m hm

private lemma divisorVal_sub {D : Y.CurveDivisor} {W : Y.Opens}

/-- The underlying rational function of the two-cover restriction-difference of a pair of
sections of `𝒪(D')` on the π-charts: restriction preserves values, so the difference map
computes the literal difference in `K(Y)`. -/
private lemma divisorVal_moduleDiff (D' : Y.CurveDivisor)
    (t : ((Y.divisorSheaf K D').obj.obj (op (fiberChart₀ π)))
      × ((Y.divisorSheaf K D').obj.obj (op (fiberChart₁ π)))) :
    divisorVal K ((Y.twoCoverSquare (fiberChart₀ π) (fiberChart₁ π)
        (preimage_chartOpen_sup π)).moduleDiff (Y.divisorSheaf K D') t)
      = divisorVal K t.1 - divisorVal K t.2 := by
  have hov : ((fiberChart₀ π ⊓ fiberChart₁ π : Y.Opens) : Set Y).Nonempty :=
    ⟨genericPoint Y, genericPoint_mem_preimage_inf π⟩
  have h1 : divisorVal K
      (((Y.divisorSheaf K D').obj.map
        (Y.twoCoverSquare (fiberChart₀ π) (fiberChart₁ π)
          (preimage_chartOpen_sup π)).f₁₂.op).hom t.1) = divisorVal K t.1 :=
    divisorPresheaf_map_val K _ hov t.1
  have h2 : divisorVal K
      (((Y.divisorSheaf K D').obj.map
        (Y.twoCoverSquare (fiberChart₀ π) (fiberChart₁ π)
          (preimage_chartOpen_sup π)).f₁₃.op).hom t.2) = divisorVal K t.2 :=
    divisorPresheaf_map_val K _ hov t.2
  rw [GrothendieckTopology.MayerVietorisSquare.moduleDiff_apply, divisorVal_sub, h1, h2]

omit [IsAffineHom π] in
/-- **The range of the two-cover difference map is the fiber lattice** (the general-`F`
restatement of the landed structure-sheaf `range_diff_eq` of
`AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.Finiteness`, assigned to FLV-2 by the worksheet §2.3): a
section of `𝒪(D + n·F)` on the overlap is a difference of restrictions from `V₀` and `V₁`
exactly when its underlying rational function lies in
`Aₙ = 𝒪(D + n·F)(V₀) ⊔ 𝒪(D + n·F)(V₁)`. -/
private lemma range_moduleDiff_eq_comap (D : Y.CurveDivisor) (n : ℕ) :
    LinearMap.range ((Y.twoCoverSquare (fiberChart₀ π) (fiberChart₁ π)
        (preimage_chartOpen_sup π)).moduleDiff
        (Y.divisorSheaf K (D + n • fiberWeilDivisor π)))
      = (fiberLattice π D n).comap
          (divisorSections K (D + n • fiberWeilDivisor π)
            (fiberChart₀ π ⊓ fiberChart₁ π)).subtype := by
  refine le_antisymm ?_ ?_
  · rintro y ⟨t, rfl⟩
    have hmem : divisorVal K ((Y.twoCoverSquare (fiberChart₀ π) (fiberChart₁ π)
          (preimage_chartOpen_sup π)).moduleDiff
          (Y.divisorSheaf K (D + n • fiberWeilDivisor π)) t) ∈ fiberLattice π D n := by
      rw [divisorVal_moduleDiff π (D + n • fiberWeilDivisor π) t]
      exact Submodule.sub_mem _ (Submodule.mem_sup_left (divisorVal_mem K t.1))
        (Submodule.mem_sup_right (divisorVal_mem K t.2))
    exact hmem
  · intro y hy
    have hy' : divisorVal K y ∈ fiberLattice π D n := hy
    obtain ⟨a, ha, b, hb, hab⟩ := Submodule.mem_sup.mp hy'
    refine ⟨((⟨a, ha⟩ : divisorSections K (D + n • fiberWeilDivisor π) (fiberChart₀ π)),
      (⟨-b, Submodule.neg_mem _ hb⟩ :
        divisorSections K (D + n • fiberWeilDivisor π) (fiberChart₁ π))), ?_⟩
    refine divisorSection_ext K ?_
    rw [divisorVal_moduleDiff π (D + n • fiberWeilDivisor π)]
    have hfin : a - (-b) = divisorVal K y := by
      rw [sub_neg_eq_add]
      exact hab
    exact hfin

/-- Mapping the comap of a submodule along `LinearEquiv.ofEq` of equal submodules is the
comap along the other subtype. -/
private lemma map_ofEq_comap_subtype {R : Type u} {M : Type v} [Ring R] [AddCommGroup M]
    [Module R M] {p q : Submodule R M} (h : p = q) (A : Submodule R M) :
    Submodule.map (LinearEquiv.ofEq p q h : p →ₗ[R] q) (A.comap p.subtype)
      = A.comap q.subtype := by
  subst h
  rw [LinearEquiv.ofEq_rfl]
  simp

/-- **The H¹-quotient identification** (FLV-2(b), the carrier): the degree-one cohomology
of the twisted divisor sheaf `𝒪(D + n·F)` is the quotient of the **fixed** ambient overlap
lattice `N = 𝒪(D)(V₀ ⊓ V₁)` by the fiber lattice `Aₙ` viewed inside `N`. Composite of the
two-cover carrier `Scheme.twoCoverH1LinearEquiv` (its affine vanishing instances
discharged by the `QcohOn` packaging of `AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.FLVQcoh`), the
range identification `range (moduleDiff) = Aₙ`, and the overlap-constancy
`𝒪(D + n·F)(V₀ ⊓ V₁) = N` of `AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.FLVLattice`. -/

    Sheaf.HModule (Y.divisorSheaf K (D + n • fiberWeilDivisor π)) 1 ≃ₗ[K]
      (divisorSections K D (fiberChart₀ π ⊓ fiberChart₁ π)
        ⧸ fiberLatticeOverlap π D n) :=
  haveI : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule'
      (Y.divisorSheaf K (D + n • fiberWeilDivisor π)) (fiberChart₀ π) 1) :=
    (isAffineOpen_preimage_chartOpen π 0).subsingleton_hModule'_divisorSheaf_one K _
  haveI : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule'
      (Y.divisorSheaf K (D + n • fiberWeilDivisor π)) (fiberChart₁ π) 1) :=
    (isAffineOpen_preimage_chartOpen π 1).subsingleton_hModule'_divisorSheaf_one K _
  (Scheme.twoCoverH1LinearEquiv K Y (fiberChart₀ π) (fiberChart₁ π)
      (Y.divisorSheaf K (D + n • fiberWeilDivisor π)) (preimage_chartOpen_sup π)).trans
    ((Submodule.quotEquivOfEq _ _ (range_moduleDiff_eq_comap π D n)).trans
      (Submodule.Quotient.equiv _ _
        (LinearEquiv.ofEq _ _ (divisorSections_add_nsmul_fiberWeilDivisor_overlap π D n))
        (map_ofEq_comap_subtype
          (divisorSections_add_nsmul_fiberWeilDivisor_overlap π D n)
          (fiberLattice π D n))))

/-!
# The fiber twist `Θₙ` of a finite map to the projective line

For the curve bundle `Y` (integral, smooth of relative dimension one and quasi-compact over
a field `K`) equipped with a **dominant** morphism `π : Y ⟶ ℙ¹`, this file pins the
Wave-4 twist datum: the divisor class of `n · (fiber of π)` and its two-cover triviality
*by construction*.

## The fiber-divisor design decision

The overlap of the pinned affine two-cover `V₀ = π⁻¹ D₊(X₀)`, `V₁ = π⁻¹ D₊(X₁)` is the
basic open of the **pulled-back chart-0 coordinate** `t₀ = π* (X₁/X₀) ∈ Γ(Y, V₀)`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.preimage_inf_eq_basicOpen_fiberCoord`, the public re-derivation of the
`private` lemma of `Cohomology.Finiteness`). The section `t₀` is regular on all of `V₀` —
its germ at every point is a nonzero element of the domain stalk, since `t₀` is a unit at the
generic point (`π` dominant) — and is a **unit exactly on the overlap** `V₀ ⊓ V₁`. Its zero
locus on `V₀` is the fiber of `π` over the point `[1 : 0]` (where `X₁` vanishes).

We therefore pin the fiber divisor of `Θₙ` as the local-equation system **on the pinned
cover itself**: the equation `t₀ⁿ` on the chart `V₀` and the constant `1` on `V₁`. The
transition cocycle between the two charts is then the two-cover unit cocycle
`gₙ = t₀ⁿ|_{V₀ ⊓ V₁}` — trivial (a single global regular equation) on each chart by
construction. This is the fiber-twist normalization certified in
`informal/w4-datum-design.md` §2(a).

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.fiberCoord` — the pulled-back chart-0 coordinate `t₀ ∈ Γ(Y, V₀)`.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.preimage_inf_eq_basicOpen_fiberCoord` — the overlap is `Y.basicOpen t₀`
  (public form of the `private` `Cohomology.Finiteness` seam).
* `AlgebraicGeometry.isUnit_fiberCoord_res_inf` — `t₀` restricts to a unit on the overlap:
  the two-cover-unit-cocycle certificate.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.fiberDivisor` — the local-equation system `(t₀ⁿ on V₀, 1 on V₁)`
  for `n · (fiber of π)`, a `Y.LocalEquations`.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.fiberTwist` — the Picard class `Θₙ = 𝒪(n · fiber) = (fiberDivisor n).picClass`.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.fiberTwist_succ`, `AlgebraicGeometry.fiberTwist_pow` — the twist is the
  `n`-th power of the unit twist: `Θₙ = Θ₁ⁿ`.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.classDeg_fiberTwist` — the degree scales linearly,
  `deg Θₙ = n · deg Θ₁` (the `= n · deg π` normalization is a *frontier*; see the note there).
-/

  pole-existence obligation, discharged from surjectivity of the finite dominant `π`.
-/
